{{short description|American mathematician|bot=PearBOT 5}}
'''Theodore James "Ted" Courant''' is an American mathematician who has conducted research in the fields of [[differential geometry]] and [[classical mechanics]].  In particular, he made seminal contributions to the study of Dirac manifolds,<ref>Courant, Ted, and Alan Weinstein, ''[http://math.berkeley.edu/~alanw/Beyond.pdf Beyond Poisson structures]''  ([[PDF]])</ref><ref>Courant, Theodore James, ''Dirac manifolds'', Trans. Amer. Math. Soc., 319:631-661, (1990).</ref> which generalize both [[symplectic manifold]]s and [[Poisson manifold]]s, and are related to the [[Dirac bracket|Dirac theory of constraints]] in physics.  Some mathematical objects in this field have since been named after him, including the [[Courant bracket]] and [[Courant algebroid]].

==Education and career==
Courant received his B.A. degree from [[Reed College]],<ref name=wildwood>{{cite web|url=https://www.wildwood.org/cf_news/view.cfm?newsid=5019|title=Admin/Faculty Additions and Changes for 2018-2019 School Year|publisher=[[Wildwood School]]|access-date=2023-08-06}}</ref> and his Ph.D. from [[The University of California, Berkeley]], where he was a student of [[Alan Weinstein]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=32763}}</ref>

After teaching at the [[University of California, Santa Cruz]] and the [[University of Minnesota]], Courant moved to secondary education at private schools in California including [[The Branson School]] and [[Wildwood School]].<ref name=wildwood/>

==Personal life==
Ted Courant is the grandson of [[Richard Courant]].<ref>{{cite web|title = Baseball Families and Math Families |author=Bill Gasarch| url = http://blog.computationalcomplexity.org/2009/02/baseball-families-and-math-families.html|date=February 12, 2009|access-date=August 7, 2023}}</ref>
